title: Semiconductor Sales Surges 103% To US$957 Billion In First Eight Months
source_used: Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) press release of 5 Oct 2026, with Evertiq (7 Oct 2026) as a second read
key_facts: SIA announced on 5 Oct 2026 that global semiconductor sales were $159.7 billion in August 2026.
That is 8% above July ($147.9 billion) and 144.3% above August 2025 ($65.4 billion).
Monthly sales are compiled by WSTS (World Semiconductor Trade Statistics) and are three-month moving averages.
SIA CEO Michael Robbins said annual global semiconductor sales have already passed $1 trillion through August, for the first time ever.
August was the 18th consecutive month of growth.
Year-to-year growth in August by region: Americas 180.9%, Asia Pacific/All Other 143.0%, China 131.3%, Europe 98.5%, Japan 62.3%.
quote_evidence: Annual global semiconductor sales have already surpassed $1 trillion through August, reaching this major milestone for the first time ever,
Monthly sales are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization and represent a three-month moving average.
SIA expects global semiconductor sales to exceed USD 1.6 trillion for the full year 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: Chip sales passing $1 trillion in eight months shows how fast AI-driven demand is growing the industry that makes the processors and memory behind AI.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (SIA release); the pool link was a BusinessToday Malaysia re-run of 11 Oct 2026.
notes: The pool link (BusinessToday Malaysia, 11 Oct 2026) returned HTTP 403, so the SAME story was read from the SIA press release (the original) and Evertiq. The pool headline gave US$957 billion and 103%; those numbers do not match SIA's official figures (over $1 trillion year to date; August up 144.3% year on year) and could not be checked, so they are not used. Event is older than today's window (5 Oct 2026).
